draft.title: The Quran and Hadith
card: The Quran is the sacred text of Islam. Muslims believe it is the word of God, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad over about 23 years.
The Hadith are records of the sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad. They were passed on by people who knew him and later written down.
The Quran is the first source of guidance for Muslims. The Hadith are used alongside it to show how the Prophet lived out its teachings.
Muslims therefore turn to the Hadith for guidance on practice, such as how the Prophet carried out acts of worship.
draft.remember: The Quran is God's word. The Hadith show how the Prophet lived and guide practice.

a.q: What do Muslims believe about the source of the Quran?
opts: It is the word of God revealed to Muhammad
It is Muhammad's own teaching in his words
It is a record of the Prophet's daily actions
It is a collection of sayings from his companions
a.why: Muslims believe God revealed the Quran to Muhammad, so it is God's word. The Hadith, not the Quran, record what the Prophet said and did.
a.clue: Think about who Muslims believe is the speaker of the Quran.

b.q: Amira wants to know how the Prophet Muhammad carried out an act of worship. Which source should she turn to?
opts: The Hadith, which record his actions
The Quran, which records his daily actions
The Quran, because the Hadith are not used
The Hadith, because they are God's revealed word
b.why: The Hadith record the actions and sayings of the Prophet, and Muslims use them to guide practice. The Quran is the first source, but the card shows it is the word of God, not a record of his actions.
b.clue: Which source records what the Prophet did?

a.best: It is the word of God revealed to Muhammad

b.best: The Hadith, which record his actions
